EXPLANATION: The experimental spectrum shows clear aromatic features: a strong C=C ring band at 1614 cm⁻¹, CH‐stretching around 3014 cm⁻¹, and multiple out-of-plane C–H bends at 755–920 cm⁻¹.  The intense doublet at 1220/1242 cm⁻¹ together with bands at 1073/1087 cm⁻¹ and 1368/1466 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of a phenol bearing an amino substituent (C–O and C–N stretches plus ring modes).  A medium OH/NH stretch appears at 3368 cm⁻¹, matching the presence of both –OH and –NH groups.  

Among the candidates, only molecule 3 (CCc1ccc(N)o1) is an aromatic phenol with an amino group and an ethyl substituent, consistent with all of these key bands, while lacking strong nitrile (≈2250 cm⁻¹) or carbonyl (≈1700–1750 cm⁻¹) stretches that would be expected for several other candidates.  Therefore candidate 3 best fits the observed Raman peaks.
